definition: A no-AI label is a label used on a product to signify that it was not made using generative AI.
details: Phrases on the labels include but are not limited to "human-made", "proudly human" and "AI-free". Some organisations that provide the labels allow product creators to download and use their no-AI labels for free, while others charge creators for analysing the content and allowing the use of the labels if the organisation believes that no AI was used.

explainer.lead: A no-AI label marks a product as not made using generative AI. It matters as a way for creators to signal human-made provenance to buyers.

tiers.eli5: It's a sticker on a product saying a person made it, not an AI.
tiers.practitioner: Creators obtain labels from organisations, some offering free downloads and others charging to analyse content before allowing label use. A pitfall is that paid labels rest on the organisation's assessment that no AI was used, not on automatic proof.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula; labels carry phrases such as "human-made", "proudly human" and "AI-free", and issuance terms vary by organisation.

explainer.example: A maker could download a free "AI-free" label, or pay an organisation to analyse the product and permit the label if it judges no AI was used.
